messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered 1 High p99 and increased 5xx rate on Dedicated pool eu-prod. Alert ID: A-9082-v2. Root TS: 1932104567
oncall-bot: Observed: 5xx up to 4.6%, queue_depth rising above baseline, autoscaler at max replicas. Suggested triage: confirm customer activity, consider temporary burst enable or route-level throttles.
maria.g: I'm taking primary. Pulling up pool dashboard and recent scaling events. Anyone see correlated deploys?
jonathan: No infra deploys. Traces show several long-running multi-request jobs from two large tenants (cust-alpha, cust-delta) starting ~13:09 UTC. They look like mass-cache-warm flows hitting long-context models.
kevin: Paging product-support for customer confirmation. @product-support can you check whether these jobs are expected?
product-support: Confirmed: cust-alpha submitted a large migration workload at ~13:05 UTC and it's churning many routes. They've logged a ticket; marking as P1 and notifying their account team.
alice: Pool state: reserved_capacity at 78%, autoscaler at configured ceiling. Burst pool available but currently offline. We can spin up an immediate +6 GPU burst which should help. Need decision on rate limiting for non-enterprise.
sre-lead: Priority: enable burst first to buy time. Only apply rate limits to non-enterprise customers if burst doesn't reduce error rate in 3 minutes. @maria.g please prepare the burst command and timing.
maria.g: Estimating node warm-up: ~75120s per GPU; for +6 GPUs full warm-up ~315 min. Draft CLI command below:
```
# rcli example
rcli dedicated toggle-burst --pool eu-prod --enable true --add-gpus 6 --reason "autoscale hit ceiling during customer migration" --expires 20m
```
jonathan: While burst comes up, I propose a soft traffic-shaping rule targeted at free/standard tiers to reduce background noise: concurrency limit 2 and token rate 1r/s with small burst. This preserves enterprise traffic.
alice: Need exact rule syntax so Console config can be applied safely. Jonathan?
jonathan: Traffic Shaper rule: selector: region==eu && customer_tier!=enterprise -> set: concurrency=2, rate=1/s, burst=3, ttl=10m. Will tag rule as ephemeral.
kevin: Applying traffic shaper rule now via Console with 15s ramp. Also will enable burst via rcli.
kevin: rcli submitted. Burst provisioning started.
maria.g: Burst add: 2/6 ready, warming KV caches. Monitoring warm-up logs.
jonathan: Slight improvement already: queue depth trending down, p99 dropping from 2600ms to 1400ms. 5xx from 4.6% -> 2.7%.
kevin: 6/6 nodes online. Telemetry shows primed caches. p99 at ~950ms, 5xx at 0.7%.
sre-lead: Good work. Hold on broader rate limits. Keep ephemeral traffic-shaper for 10m. @product-support coordinate with cust-alpha to stop mass-run.
product-support: Reached out; cust-alpha paused the job and will reschedule to off-peak. Account team acknowledged.
maria.g: We'll let the burst expire at 20m by default; removing traffic-shaper after 10m if stable. Filing follow-ups for autoscaler tuning and customer isolation.
jonathan: Follow-up plan: 1) monitor metrics for 10m 2) if relapse, extend burst or increase reserved capacity 3) create ticket to isolate heavy customers into sub-pools (noisy-neighbor mitigation).
kevin: Tagged pool with 'mitigation-incident-1932104567' and recorded CLI run for audit. Updating incident notes in Console.
sre-lead: Handoff: @jonathan owns the tuning ticket and follow-up cost analysis. @maria.g to compile postmortem and timeline. Oncall evening team take over in 30m.
jonathan: Creating ENG-2379: "Increase burst buffer and introduce per-customer sub-pools for eu-prod" with proposed config and cost estimate.
maria.g: Drafting postmortem with timeline, exact commands executed, telemetry graphs and recommendations on autoscaler ceiling.
product-support: Cust-alpha confirms they will include Redwood in migration runbooks next time. They apologized and will schedule during low traffic.
kevin: Metrics stable for 18m. Will close mitigation after 20m of stability. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident A-9082-v2 -> mitigated via burst + traffic-shaper. Reminder: submit follow-up for autoscaler thresholds and burst sizing.
